title: Cathode rays
content: Cathode rays are fast moving electrons emitted from the cathode of a discharge tube.

title: X-rays
content: X-rays are electromagnetic waves like light, but their wavelengths are much shorter than those of light.

title: Photoelectric effect
content: When electromagnetic radiation (e.g. light) of sufficient energy incident on the metal surface then electrons are ejected from its surface. This phenomenon is known as photoelectric effect.

title: Isotopes
content: Isotopes are the atoms of the same element with different masses.

title: Redshift
content: In astronomy, this shift toward longer wavelengths is referred to as a redshift since red is at the long-wavelength end of the visible spectrum.

title: Hubble time
content: The Hubble time or age of the universe is defined as the reciprocal of the Hubble constant.
